title: Generative AI and the temporary upskilling of knowledge workers
title_zh: 生成式人工智能与知识工作者的临时技能提升
abstract: Upskilling often refers to the process by which workers acquire and expand their skills, enabling them to perform different types of work as market demands change. Here we demonstrate that generative artificial intelligence can act as an ‘exoskeleton’, enhancing workers’ capabilities when attempting new skills, but these gains depend on continued technology use. We run a randomized controlled trial on upskilling by providing management consultants (N = 487) access and training in using ChatGPT to solve data science tasks outside their skill sets, which cannot be independently solved by ChatGPT. The treated workers scored higher than the control group on three tasks, although we can reject the hypothesis that they performed as well as expert data scientists. We find no evidence that treated workers are better at answering technical questions without ChatGPT post-experiment, suggesting that their demonstrated technical capabilities do not imply knowledge acquisition. This randomized trial by Wiles et al. shows that generative AI helps knowledge workers perform data science tasks outside their skill set, but workers do not retain the underlying knowledge when the tool is removed.
abstract_zh: 技能提升通常是指工人在市场需求变化时获取和扩展技能，以执行不同类型的工作。在此，我们展示生成式人工智能可以作为‘外骨骼’，在工人尝试新技能时增强其能力，但这些提升取决于持续的技术使用。我们在随机对照试验中研究了技能提升的问题，向487名管理顾问提供了使用ChatGPT解决其技能范围之外的数据科学任务的权限和培训，这些任务ChatGPT无法独立完成。接受处理的工作者在三项任务中的得分均高于对照组，尽管我们可以拒绝假设他们表现得像专家数据科学家一样好。我们发现没有证据表明，实验后无ChatGPT辅助时，处理组工作者在技术问题上的回答更好，这表明他们的展示能力并不意味着知识获取。Wiles等人的这项随机试验表明，生成式人工智能有助于知识工作者完成其技能范围之外的数据科学任务，但当工具被移除时，工作者不会保留底层知识。
